facts.text: Viking 1 Lander was deployed at Chryse Planitia during Viking 1 in 1976.

The Viking 1 lander operated on the surface of Mars for over six years, from July 1976 to November 1982. It was the first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars and return images from the surface. The lander carried biology experiments, a gas chromatograph mass spectrometer, and cameras that captured the first colour photos from the Martian surface.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Performed the first direct chemical analysis of Martian soil and conducted three biology experiments designed to detect metabolic signs of life.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Chryse Planitia.
Silent since November 1982, the lander remains intact on the surface at Chryse Planitia, visible in orbital imagery from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.
